Hurt at work in BC?

WorkSafeBC physiotherapy for work injuries

WorkSafeBC asks injured workers to see a contracted physiotherapist and say the injury is work-related. Book a WCB physio assessment online at any of our 19+ locations from Vancouver to Abbotsford.

Quick answers

What injured workers ask us first

  • Can I start before my claim is accepted?

    Yes, for the first visit. A contracted physiotherapist can do your initial assessment on a pending claim, without prior approval, if it is within 60 days of your injury.

  • Will I pay anything?

    Once WorkSafeBC accepts your claim, care related to your claim is billed to WorkSafeBC and you should not have to pay fees.

  • Do I need a doctor’s referral?

    Not for physiotherapy. WorkSafeBC tells workers to go to a contracted physiotherapist and say the injury is work-related.

  • Is WCB the same as WorkSafeBC?

    Yes. WorkSafeBC is the Workers’ Compensation Board of BC, so many people call it WCB.

How it works

Three steps to WCB physio. That’s it.

You can book before you have a claim number.

  1. Right away

    Report the injury

    Tell your employer as soon as it is safe. Report to WorkSafeBC online any time, or call Teleclaim at 1.888.967.5377 (604.231.8888 in the Lower Mainland), weekdays 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.

  2. Next

    Book your assessment

    Pick the clinic nearest home or work and book a WCB Physio Initial Session online. Tell us the injury happened at work.

  3. At your visit

    Bring your claim number

    WorkSafeBC mails an 8-digit claim number. Bring it if you have it. We bill WorkSafeBC for your care.

Before you book

Is WCB physio for you?

It depends on where your claim is. Here is how each stage works.

Who this is for

Workers in BC who were hurt at work and have reported the injury to WorkSafeBC, or are reporting it now. The claim can still be pending.

Where is your claim?

  1. Accepted. Care related to your claim is billed to WorkSafeBC and you should not have to pay fees.
  2. Pending. Your first assessment can go ahead without prior approval within 60 days of your injury. WorkSafeBC pays for that assessment even if the claim is later denied. Funded treatment visits start once the claim is accepted.
  3. More than 60 days since the injury. WorkSafeBC must approve treatment before it starts. It is not refused automatically.

Have these ready Checklist

  • Your 8-digit claim number, if it has arrived
  • Your employer’s name and contact details
  • When and how the injury happened
  • Your Personal Health Number

TipBooking online? Choose WCB Physio Initial Session so your first visit is set up as a WorkSafeBC claim.

Common work injuries

Work injuries our physiotherapists treat

Your plan is built around what your job asks of your body, whether that is lifting on a site, driving, patient care or desk work.

  • Back strain from lifting

    Pain or stiffness after lifting, carrying, bending or twisting at work.

  • Shoulder strain and overuse

    Pain reaching overhead, pushing, pulling or carrying loads on one side.

  • Repetitive strain

    Wrist, elbow or forearm pain from repeated tasks, tools or keyboard work.

  • Neck strain

    Neck pain and stiffness after a strain, a long shift at a screen or a sudden movement.

  • Slips, trips and falls

    Sprains, strains and bruising after a fall on stairs, ladders, ice or wet floors.

  • Knee and ankle injuries

    Twists and sprains from climbing, kneeling, uneven ground or jumping down.

Your first visit

What happens at your WCB physio assessment

  • We ask how and when you were hurt at work, and what your job involves.
  • Your physiotherapist checks how you move, your strength and where it hurts.
  • You get a plan with goals tied to the tasks you need to get back to.
  • You leave with things you can do at home and at work while you recover.

Bring your claim number if you have it, and wear clothes you can move in.

Return to work

Back to work, one step at a time

  1. Phase 1

    Assess

    We look at your injury and the physical demands of your job.

  2. Phase 2

    Treat

    Hands-on care and exercise to settle pain and restore movement.

  3. Phase 3

    Build

    Graded exercise that works up to the lifting, standing or reaching your job needs.

  4. Phase 4

    Return

    Back to work, sometimes on modified duties first, with a plan for the rest.

If you need more treatment, your physiotherapist can ask WorkSafeBC for it. WorkSafeBC decides. Read more: Returning to work after a workplace injury

FAQ

WorkSafeBC physio questions

Is WCB the same as WorkSafeBC?

Yes. WorkSafeBC is the Workers’ Compensation Board of British Columbia, which is why many people still call it WCB. You will see both names on our booking pages.

Do I need a claim number before I book?

No. At a WorkSafeBC-contracted physiotherapist you can have your initial assessment before WorkSafeBC accepts your claim. You do need to report the injury to WorkSafeBC so there is a claim to bill, even if it is still pending. WorkSafeBC mails you an 8-digit claim number once it gets your report. Bring it to a later visit if you do not have it yet.

Do I need a doctor’s referral for WorkSafeBC physio?

No. WorkSafeBC’s guidance for workers is to visit a contracted physiotherapist and explain that the injury is work-related. A doctor’s referral is not one of the steps. Massage therapy is different: it needs a doctor’s referral and an accepted claim.

Will I have to pay anything?

Once WorkSafeBC accepts your claim, your provider bills WorkSafeBC for care related to your claim and you should not have to pay any fees. If you have treatment before your claim is accepted, a clinic may ask you to pay, and you can ask for a refund if the claim is accepted later. Ask the clinic how it handles visits while your claim is pending before you book follow-up visits.

What happens if my claim is denied?

If your claim was pending at your first visit, WorkSafeBC still pays the contracted clinic for that initial assessment, even if the claim is later denied. WorkSafeBC does not pay for treatment visits given while the claim was pending if it is denied.

It has been more than 60 days since my injury. Can I still get physio?

Yes, but WorkSafeBC has to approve treatment first when it starts more than 60 days after the injury. It is not refused automatically. Call the clinic and we will tell you what we need to ask WorkSafeBC.

How many physio visits does WorkSafeBC cover?

WorkSafeBC sets the length of each treatment period for your claim. If you need more treatment, your physiotherapist can ask WorkSafeBC for it, and WorkSafeBC decides. We explain what is approved for your claim at each stage.

What if I go to a physio who is not contracted with WorkSafeBC?

You pay for each visit yourself and ask WorkSafeBC to reimburse you at its set rate, which is $95 per visit from April 1, 2026. You pay any difference.

Can I get massage therapy on my WorkSafeBC claim?

Yes, with a doctor’s referral and an accepted claim. WorkSafeBC covers an assessment and up to 6 massage treatments in the first 8 weeks after the injury without pre-approval. More needs approval. See the clinic list below for clinics that book WCB massage online.

How do I report a workplace injury to WorkSafeBC?

Tell your employer as soon as it is safe, and tell anyone who treats you that it happened at work. Then report it to WorkSafeBC online at any time, or by phone through Teleclaim. Teleclaim is 1.888.967.5377 toll-free or 604.231.8888 in the Lower Mainland, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. You have up to one year to report, but report right away.
